definition: Lasting for a very short time; fleeting.
etymology: From Greek ephēmeros (“lasting only a day”).

example_sentences.sentence: The beauty of the sunset was ephemeral, gone in minutes.
Fame can be ephemeral when it depends on trends.

mnemonic: “Ephi-meral” → “a MERELY a day” kind of lasting.

definition: Sweet or musical; pleasant to hear.

example_sentences.sentence: Her mellifluous voice made the narration hypnotic.
The violin produced a mellifluous, warm tone.

definition: A subtle difference in meaning, expression, or tone.

example_sentences.sentence: Good writers understand the nuance between similar words.
Her tone carried a nuance of disappointment.

mnemonic: Nuance = “new-ants” — tiny details you might miss.

definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
etymology: From Latin meticulosus (“timid, fearful”), later “overly careful.”

example_sentences.sentence: She kept meticulous notes during the meeting.
The lab requires meticulous handling of samples.

mnemonic: Meticulous = “metric” + “ticks” — you measure every tiny tick.
